newsitem.title: USA: Pacific Scientific served with complaint.
newsitem.headline: Pacific Scientific served with complaint.

text.p: Pacific Scientific Co said Thursday it has received a complaint alleging that it and Chief Executive Officer Edgar S. Brower made false and misleading statements regarding its Solium subsidiary.

The complaint, filed in the United States District Court for the Central District of California, seeks damages on behalf of an individual who on April 10, 1996 purchased, 20 of the company's 7 3/4% convertible subordinated debentures due 2003, it said.

The company also said that relief is sought for all other persons who purchased similar debentures between October 3, 1994 and July 2, 1996, a period during which the complaint alleges the price of the debentures was "artificially inflated." These debentures were originally issued by the company in 1983 and are traded on the New York Exchange.

The complaint is based on substantially the same allegations as a similar complaint received on October 23, 1996 on behalf of an individual who purchased the company's common stock, Pacific Scientific said. The periods of purchases of common stock and debentures for which relief is sought are identical in both complaints, it said.
Pacific Scientific and Brower denied the allegations and said they will vigorously defend against the action.

The company designs, manufactures and markets electrical equipment and safety equipment. The Solium subsidiary is involved in designing, manufacturing and distributing electronic ballast and adaptors for fluorescent lamps.
